groups.name: One bookmarkable viewer port per repo
groups.label: PORT
groups.reason: A repo with no saved viewer port got 53366 or a random port and the computed port was never saved, so the bookmarkable address could drift. Pick a deterministic per-repo slot once, save it on first viewer start, recover it from viewer state, fail loudly when occupied, and write the rule in the skill.

verify.method: Temp-state real viewer: rollover, restart, upgrade and registry repair keep the repo port and serve the newest list; deterministic slot skips other repos; occupied port fails; live 127.0.0.1:58771 still serves #123.

findings.title: A fresh change list cannot record a post-merge Introspect
findings.summary: After a pull request merges, the next list refuses Collect until a post-merge Introspect is recorded, but there is no supported command that can record one on that fresh list.
findings.impact: Operators cannot start Collect on the next list without writing the tracker by hand, which is forbidden.
findings.recommendation: Add a supported bcl introspect --scope post_merge that records the post-merge Introspect on a new list that has not reached Verify, drafts and checks coverage from the merged list's job data, and does not mark the new list as having finished ordinary Introspect.
findings.done_when: An official command records the post-merge Introspect on a new list that has not finished Verify, collection can then start, and a test covers this without a hand-edited tracker.
findings.observed: On list 123, bcl start failed with Collect is refused until the post-merge Introspect is recorded. bcl introspect has no --scope flag, and manage_findings require_transition introspect requires Verify. A script then copied 122 tracking.post_merge_introspect onto 123.json through manage_findings.write; that was a direct tracker write, not a supported bcl command.

details.command: bcl introspect --scope post_merge --draft FILE.json, then bcl introspect --scope post_merge --sections FILE.json
details.gap: require_transition introspect requires verify; CLI has no --scope; official introspect would also mark stages_reached and close the plan

findings.title: Developer observability does not capture Cursor CLI runs
findings.summary: Codex jobs are recorded automatically, but Cursor CLI headless runs are not, so their model, tokens, time and plan refusals have to be written down by hand.
findings.impact: Change-list jobs and model bake-offs run on the Cursor CLI have no trustworthy usage numbers, and refusals such as running out of usage are easy to miss.
findings.recommendation: Capture Cursor CLI runs by default through a Cursor hook plus Cursor's own JSON result, and add a read-back command like the Codex one.

findings.summary: Fix work done directly by a helper, not through a coding tool, is recorded as a failed fix.
findings.impact: Lanes look failed and the failure streak grows even when the fix is good; parallel lanes in one folder can be credited with each other's commits.

findings.recommendation: Owned by the batched-change-list plugin: compare lane-scoped files or accept a commit sha argument; allow finding adds while a job runs.

findings.title: Passing test lines that mention 'error' are counted as failures
findings.summary: The log reader treats a passing test whose name or text contains the word error as a failure.
findings.impact: Healthy test runs raise false failure alerts.
findings.done_when: A passing test line (node ✔, TAP 'ok N', and similar pass marks) is never counted as a failure, even if the test name or assertion text contains 'error'.
findings.observed: iter_textlog in sources.py marks a line as log_error when _LOG_ERROR matches \b(error|exception|traceback|fatal|failed|failure)\b (case-insensitive) and the line does not contain status=ok. Pytest failures have their own parser; generic text logs do not skip pass marks. In the Likeminded collect of /tmp/bcl-r1/obs-r3 at 09:47 IST 25 Nov 2026, the passing node spec line '✔ unknown routes return a JSON not_found error' was reported as log_error/log failed 1x.
findings.recommendation: Skip known pass/success lines before the keyword check; status=ok alone is not enough.

findings.title: A repo tracker port can still change or be picked at random
findings.summary: A repo with no saved viewer port gets the shared default port if free, otherwise a random port, and the fixed-port rule is not written in the skill, so a bookmarked tracker address is not guaranteed to keep showing the newest list.
findings.impact: Guru cannot rely on one bookmark per repo to always show the latest PR list; a new repo can land on a random port or take another repo's usual port.
findings.done_when: A repo's viewer port is chosen once (deterministic, never colliding with another repo's saved port), stored, and kept through rollover, viewer restart, plugin upgrade and registry repair; a new list for the same repo takes over that port and serves the newest list; a collision fails loudly instead of moving ports; the rule is written in the skill; tests cover all of this.
findings.observed: 25 Nov 2026 13:48 IST, Guru: the tracker must keep one assigned port per repo so it can be bookmarked. Today agent-plugins is 58771 (registry saves viewer_port 58771 for #121, #122, #123) and Likeminded is 53366. Code at r13 ead254f4: live_state._project_port picks 53366 if free, otherwise port 0 (random) when a repo has no saved port; serve.py defaults --port to 53366; SKILL.md has no rule; viewer.md still says choose another available port; no test proves a rollover or restart to a new list keeps the repo port and serves the newest list.
findings.recommendation: Derive a deterministic per-repo port (hash slot, skipping other repos' saved ports), persist it on first viewer start, fall back to the repo viewer state on registry repair, make serve.py --port required, and write the rule in SKILL.md and viewer.md with tests.

details.related: BCL-94 (verified_fixed, archived): per-project fixed port; this covers the remaining gaps

findings.title: Registry updates can overwrite each other when two change-list commands run at once
findings.summary: Every registry update reads the whole registry, changes one record and writes it back with no lock, so two commands that update it at the same moment can drop each other's change.
findings.impact: A rollover, adoption or saved viewer port written by one command can be silently lost when another command saves the registry at the same time.
findings.done_when: Concurrent registry updates never lose a change; a test runs two updates at once and both survive.
findings.observed: 25 Nov 2026 (IST), BCL-185 review (OpenCode deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, R2-PORT): live_state.save_registry and its callers (locate adopt, register_rollover, the rollover_pending clear in bin/bcl, and the new first-start port save) do read-modify-write of registry.json without tracker_lock; only the per-tracker file is locked.
findings.recommendation: Hold an exclusive lock on the registry across read, change and write (tracker_lock), and re-read inside the lock.

details.source finding: Left over from the BCL-185 post-fix review notes; filed as its own finding per the plan-review follow-up rule.

findings.title: Old per-list viewer files are never cleaned up, and a reused process id makes one look running
findings.summary: Viewer files from lists that used one viewer per list stay in the state folder forever, and the liveness check only asks whether their recorded process id exists, so a reused id makes a long-dead viewer look alive.
findings.impact: Stale viewer files clutter the state folder and can steer a new repo's first port pick away from a free port.
findings.done_when: Old per-list viewer files whose viewer is gone are removed or ignored, and a viewer counts as running only when its own health check answers with its recorded identity; a test covers a reused process id.
findings.observed: 25 Nov 2026 (IST), BCL-185 plan review (OpenCode deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, R2-PORT): ~/.agents/state/batched-change-list/viewers still holds ingpoc--agent-plugins--107/110/111/112/113/114/115/121.json with dead pids beside the per-repo files; live_state._state_is_live uses _pid_is_running (os.kill(pid, 0)), so a recycled pid makes such a file reserve its port during a fresh pick.
findings.recommendation: Check liveness through the recorded port's /__bcl_health instance, and prune dead per-list viewer files when the per-repo file exists.

findings.title: The observability viewer opens an older numbered list instead of the live one
findings.summary: When a project has both a numbered list and a live list with a non-numeric id, the viewer picks the higher number as the latest list, so the live list is hidden by default.
findings.impact: Guru opens a project and sees an old or merged list instead of the one being worked on.
findings.done_when: When a project has a numbered list that is merged or older and a live list with a non-numeric name, the viewer opens the live, most recently written list by default and marks it live in the picker; the agent-plugins project still opens PR #123; a test covers it.
findings.observed: 25 Nov 2026 ~14:05 IST, DO-22 review of cb2a5ef1: _tracker_sort_key in runtime/backend/round_view.py orders by (pr number, last_written_at, mtime) with non-numeric ids as 0, so build_issues and find_tracker pick 19.json over a newer live bcl-r1.json.
findings.recommendation: Rank latest by unmerged first, then last_written_at, then pr number and mtime; keep the chronological order used for history unchanged.

findings.title: Official token totals per job and per round are missing
findings.summary: Observability records usage parts for some Cursor runs, but it does not publish a single official total per job and per round, and a missing cost is left empty instead of marked not reported.
findings.impact: Change list introspection cannot compare token cost across rounds, so waste cannot be measured.
findings.observed: On 25 Nov 2026 in the evening IST, every change list job on the current list had no token source, and the viewer had no usage series. One Cursor run had usage parts that summed to the command line total, but cost was empty.
findings.done_when: The official path publishes a total per job and per round that includes cache read, and cost is a number or is marked not reported, with tests and a live read.
findings.recommendation: Add an official usage payload and keep unsupported cost marked not reported.
